title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 224-226). Grothendieck studies a profinite group M^{!~}_{0,3}, built from solutions (xi, eta) of the 'équation des lacets' for P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. It is a Teichmüller/GT-type group of automorphisms of the profinite pi_{0,3} together with extra data. He also uses a quotient N^{!~}_{0,3}. He tests these objects against 'adelic invariants'.

The adelic image. Each element u is sent to a 2x2 matrix underline-u in GL(2, Z^). The natural source of such a map is pi_{0,3} = Gamma(2)/{±1}, the free group on (1 2; 0 1) and (1 0; 2 1). Passing to Z^ amounts to taking the congruence quotient. By (173), underline-u lies in the Borel-type subgroup B = {(mu M; 0 1)} of affine matrices. When u comes from M^{!~}_{0,3}(0), the extra condition M ≡ 0 mod 2 holds.

The subgroup L_0. L_0 is the closed (procyclic) subgroup generated by l_0 = (1 -2; 0 1). This is a generator of Gamma(2), i.e. a loop around a puncture. By (177), multiplying on the left by l_0^n replaces M by M - 2n.

This page. Let B_1 = {(mu M; 0 1) : mu in Z^*, M in 2Z^}, which is the image of M^{!~}_{0,3}[0]. Then B_1 modulo L_0 is identified with the 'maximal torus' T_0 = {(mu 0; 0 1)}. More precisely, (178) gives a semidirect product B_1 = T_0 · L_0. Here L_0 is normal, since conjugating l_0^n by diag(mu,1) gives l_0^{n mu}, and T_0 ∩ L_0 = 1.

Consequences.
- In the quotient M^{!~}_{0,3}(0)/L_0 ≅ N^{!~}_{0,3}, the only adelic invariant left, in the present setting parametrised by (alpha, beta), is the multiplier mu, i.e. the cyclotomic-type character.
- The decomposition (178) yields a canonical splitting of the extension 1 → L_0 → M^{!~}_{0,3}[0] → N^{!~}_{0,3} → 1.

Proposition. Every class ū in N^{!~}_{0,3} has a unique representative u in M^{!~}_{0,3}[0] with underline-u in T_0, i.e. M = 0. The unique n is M/2 (next page).

Equivalently, the associated xi = (A B; C D) has B = 0; Grothendieck adds that it then has the shape (* 0; 1-D D). The next page:
- calls such (xi, eta) 'normalised';
- shows that the resulting subgroup (179) is a section of the extensions of N^{!~}_{0,3} by L_0, by pi^_{0,3}, and by the larger group;
- writes every element uniquely as f^{-1} u_xi with u_xi normalised.

Purpose. This removes the indeterminacy coming from conjugation by inertia (powers of the loop around a puncture). It plays the role of Drinfeld's normalisation f in F^' (vanishing abelianised part) in the definition of GT^.
errors: The semidirect-product claim (178) and the uniqueness n = M/2 are correct. They need 2 to be a non-zero-divisor in Z^ (true): M in 2Z^ gives a unique n with M = 2n.

The bracketed claim that B = 0 forces xi = (* 0; 1-D D), i.e. C = 1 - D, cannot be checked from this page. A naive computation with xi = u·rho(u)^{-1} and rho the swap involution gives C = 0 when M = 0, not C = 1 - D. The bracket convention [u, rho] used here may differ, so this is flagged as unverified rather than as an error.
Notation is slightly inconsistent across these pages: M^{!~}_{0,3}(0) versus M^{!~}_{0,3}[0], and (179) is used twice on the next page.

ideas.what: Mapping a GT-type group of automorphisms of pi^_{0,3} = Gamma(2)^ to the congruence (adelic) quotient in GL(2,Z^), with image in the affine Borel {(mu M; 0 1)}
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT^ / G_Q on the congruence completion of Gamma(2); the image factors through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and others (Galois action on congruence quotients and modular towers), 1980s-90s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme gives only the general GT program, not this computation

ideas.what: Semidirect decomposition B_1 = T_0 ⋉ L_0 of the level-2 affine Borel subgroup of GL(2,Z^)
ideas.modern_name: Torus–unipotent (Levi) decomposition of a Borel subgroup

ideas.what: Canonical splitting of the extension of N^{!~}_{0,3} by the inertia procyclic group L_0, by choosing the representative whose adelic image has M = 0 ('normalised' (xi, eta))
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of GT elements (lambda, f) with f in the derived subgroup F^'

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently arrives at a normalisation that removes the inertia/conjugation ambiguity in solutions of the 'équation des lacets'. He does this through an adelic (congruence-quotient) criterion, M = 0 in the Borel image, rather than Drinfeld's abelianisation criterion f in F^'. This is a variant of the known normalisation, documented in his own formalism; it is not a new theorem.
missed.quote: on trouve grâce à la décomposition (178) dans GL(2, Z^) un scindage canonique de l'extension M_{0,3}^{!~}(0) de N_{0,3}^{!~} par L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence of how Grothendieck approached the structure of GT^ via level-2 congruence data. It may interest historians comparing his program with Drinfeld and Ihara.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an elementary but clean structural step: a semidirect decomposition and a canonical section of an extension. It parallels the standard normalisation in GT theory. It is of historical interest only, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads roughly 'matrices ξ [or] u de B telles que u ≡ 1 (2) i.e. M ≡ 0 (2)'. The leading 'pour' is struck and 'fermé' is inserted above 'ss-groupe'.
'{+L/+}tore maximal' should read '/ le tore maximal T_0 de B': the inserted word is 'le', not a script L.

The middle paragraph is very cursive. It reads approximately 'le seul invariant adélique qui reste dans le contexte présent (quand on raisonne dans le contexte présent, paramétrisé par α, β) est le multiplicateur ... μ'. The transcription's 'arithmétique' is probably 'adélique', and its duplicated 'dans le contexte présent' matches the image's repetition.
In the Proposition, 'il existe un représentant unique u dans M_{0,3}^{!~}[0]' uses square brackets [0] here, versus (0) earlier.
'225' at the bottom left is the archive page number, not part of the text.
